newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1997 GDP goal still reachable - Istat.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1997 GDP goal still reachable - Istat.

text.p: Latest data suggests that the Italian economy is picking up, meaning that the government might still meet its target of 1.2 percent economic growth this year, the president of national statistics office Istat said.
Alberto Zuliani also told a parliamentary commission that average inflation this year should be well below the official 2.5 percent target.
He added that the official CPI target of 1.8 percent for next year was credible.
Italian inflation in May was 1.6 percent year-on-year, while in the first quarter of 1997, Italy's gross domestic product (ROSE) fell by 0.5 percent year-on-year.

"The disappointing performance of national accounts in the first quarter appears to have been mitigated by signals which show a strengthening of the Italian economy from the second quarter of 97," Zuiliani told the Senate budget commission.
"In the first quarter there were two working days less (than the same period last year). By contrast the number of working days in the second quarter should have a favourable impact on GDP," he said.
"In the light of a few forecasts...the (government) target for growth of 1.2 percent in 1997...still appears achievable," he added.

However he added that there would have to be very marked economic growth in the coming months to hit the 1.2 percent figure. Istat is due to release preliminary GDP data from the second quarter on August 29. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
